content: Hydrogen peroxide solution is an antiseptic that has been approved by the FDA for the treatment of removing secretions associated with a sore mouth. For adult patients, hydrogen peroxide solution is intended for external use only. It should be applied locally as needed. There is limited information available regarding off-label uses of hydrogen peroxide solution in adults, whether supported by guidelines or not. For pediatric patients, there is limited information regarding FDA-approved uses of hydrogen peroxide solution. Similarly, there is limited information on off-label uses in pediatric patients, whether supported by guidelines or not. Contraindications for hydrogen peroxide solution are not well-documented in the drug label. Warnings include consulting a doctor before use if the injuries involve deep or puncture wounds or serious burns. Discontinue use and seek medical advice if an infection occurs, or if redness, irritation, swelling, or pain persists or worsens. Precautions include keeping the product out of reach of children. In the event of accidental ingestion, seek professional assistance or contact a Poison Control Center immediately. Adverse reactions are not well-documented in clinical trials or postmarketing data for hydrogen peroxide solution. Drug interactions with hydrogen peroxide solution are not well-documented in the drug label. There is no FDA guidance on the use of hydrogen peroxide solution in specific populations, including pregnant women, nursing mothers, pediatric patients, geriatric patients, specific gender or racial populations, patients with renal or hepatic impairment, individuals of reproductive potential, or immunocompromised patients. Hydrogen peroxide solution is administered topically. There is limited information regarding monitoring requirements for its use. There is no information available regarding IV compatibility of hydrogen peroxide solution. Overdosage information, including chronic overdose, is not well-documented in the drug label. Pharmacological details, including the mechanism of action, structure, pharmacodynamics, pharmacokinetics, and nonclinical toxicology, are not well-documented in the drug label. Clinical studies involving hydrogen peroxide solution are not well-documented in the drug label. Information on how the product is supplied, including storage recommendations, is limited in the drug label. There is limited information available regarding patient counseling for hydrogen peroxide solution. The interaction between alcohol and hydrogen peroxide solution has not been established. Patients are advised to consult their doctor regarding the effects of consuming alcohol while using this medication. There is limited information available regarding brand names and look-alike drug names for hydrogen peroxide solution in the drug label.
